{{nihongo|'''Harina Shrine'''|針名神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Harina Shrine''' (針名神社, Harina-jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tempaku-chō Ōaza Hirabari}}, {{ill|Tenpaku-ku|Q1155245|qid=Q1155245}}, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is traditionally identified with the “Harina Shrine” of {{ill|Aichi District|Q552687|qid=Q552687|lt=Aichi District}}, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, although, as described below, there are differing theories.

=== History ===
Until the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, it was called '''Tenjin'''. The early Edo–period document {{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}} states, “Hirabari Village … Tenjin … exempt from dues,” suggesting that it was already enshrined as Tenjin by the {{ill|17th century|Q7016|qid=Q7016}}. A {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} dated {{ill|1699|Q7710|qid=Q7710}} ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 12) remains, inscribed with “Tenjingū.” Since the Edo period, the Murase family (the {{ill|Nanushi|Q110095960|qid=Q110095960}} of Hirabari Village) has served as {{ill|Shinkan (official)|Q11589454|qid=Q11589454}}.

Until the early Edo period, the shrine stood at a place called “Motogō” on the left bank of the {{ill|Tenpaku River|Q11443111|qid=Q11443111|lt=Tempaku River}} northwest of the current site. In {{ill|1612|Q6771|qid=Q6771}} ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 17), when Hirabari Village was relocated southward in connection with the improvement of the {{ill|Suruga Kaidō|Q24864271|qid=Q24864271}} by order of {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|an|Ieyasu Tokugawa|ar|توكوغاوا إيه-ياسو|arz|توكوجاوا ايه ياسو|ast|Tokugawa Ieyasu|az|Tokuqava İeyasu|ba|Токугава Иэясу|ban|Tokugawa Ieyasu|bcl|Tokugawa Ieyasu|be|Такугава Іэясу|bg|Токугава Иеясу|br|Tokugawa Ieyasu|bs|Tokugava Iejasu|ca|Tokugawa Ieyasu|cdo|Dáik-chiŏng Gă-kŏng|cs|Iejasu Tokugawa|de|Tokugawa Ieyasu|el|Τοκουγκάβα Ιεγιάσου|eo|Tokugawa Ieyasu|es|Tokugawa Ieyasu|et|Tokugawa Ieyasu|eu|Tokugawa Ieyasu|fa|توکوگاوا ایه‌یاسو|fi|Tokugawa Ieyasu|fr|Tokugawa Ieyasu|gl|Tokugawa Ieyasu|gor|Tokugawa Ieyasu|hak|Tokugawa Ieyasu|he|טוקוגאווה איאיאסו|hi|तोकुगावा इयासू|hr|Tokugava Iejasu|hu|Tokugava Iejaszu|hy|Իեյասու Տոկուգավա|id|Tokugawa Ieyasu|is|Tokugawa Ieyasu|it|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康|jv|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ka|ტოკუგავა იეიასუ|kk|Токугава Иэясу|ko|도쿠가와 이에야스|la|Ieiasus Daifusama|lt|Tokugava Iejasu|lv|Tokugava Iejasu|mg|Tokugawa Ieyasu|mn|Токүгава Иэясү|ms|Tokugawa Ieyasu|nl|Tokugawa Ieyasu|no|Tokugawa Ieyasu|oc|Tokugawa Ieyasu|pl|Ieyasu Tokugawa|pt|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ro|Ieyasu Tokugawa|ru|Токугава Иэясу|sc|Tokugawa Ieyasu|sh|Ieyasu Tokugawa|simple|Tokugawa Ieyasu|sk|Iejasu Tokugawa|sl|Tokugava Iejasu|sq|Tokugava Iejasu|sr|Токугава Ијејасу|sv|Tokugawa Ieyasu|tg|Иеясу Токугава|th|โทกูงาวะ อิเอยาซุ|tl|Tokugawa Ieyasu|tok|jan Tokukawa Ijejasu|tr|Tokugawa Ieyasu|uk|Токуґава Ієясу|ur|توکوگاوا ائیاسو|uz|Tokugava Ieyasu|vi|Tokugawa Ieyasu|war|Tokugawa Ieyasu|wuu|德川家康|zh|德川家康|zh_classical|德川家康|zh_min_nan|Tokugawa Ieyasu|zh_yue|德川家康|zu|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977}}, the shrine was also moved to its present location. Place names such as “Kanda” still remain around present-day Hirabari 1-chōme, reflecting the former sacred fields of the shrine.

{{ill|Amano Sadakage|Q6535030|qid=Q6535030}} identified this shrine with the “Harina Shrine” of Aichi District, Owari Province, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and this view subsequently became the prevailing theory. However, Amano’s basis for the identification was merely that the shrine is located in Hirabari Village of Aichi District and shares the character “hari” (針), and no munafuda bearing the name “Harina” has been found. The late Edo–period {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=local historian}} {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}} sharply criticized this identification, arguing that Hirabari Village belonged not to Aichi District but to {{ill|Yamada district, Owari|Q11470699|qid=Q11470699|lt=Yamada District}} prior to the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}. Tsuda asserted that the original “Harina Shrine” was the Tenjin Shrine in {{ill|Kasumori-chō|Q11567254|qid=Q11567254}}, {{ill|Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Q780521|qid=Q780521}}. Recent studies have also suggested that the Tempaku Ward area, including Hirabari, likely belonged to Yamada District in the medieval period, indicating that there is room for reconsideration regarding the identification of this shrine as “Harina Shrine”{{Sfn|Nagoya Local Culture Society|1982|pp=23–29}}.

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5), it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. In {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} (Meiji 42), a nearby Hachiman shrine was merged, adding {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} to the enshrined deities. nî|zh_yue|1976年|qid=Q2480}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 51) as a commemorative project celebrating the 50th anniversary of the enthronement of {{ill|Hirohito|Q34479|qid=Q34479}}. The precincts cover approximately 12,000 tsubo, making it one of the largest shrines in {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}. In {{ill|1982|ab|1982|af|1982|als|1982|am|1982 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1982|ar|1982|ary|1982|arz|1982|ast|1982|av|1982 сон|avk|1982|az|1982|azb|۱۹۸۲ (میلادی)|ba|1982 йыл|ban|1982|bar|1982|bat_smg|1982|bcl|1982|be|1982|be_x_old|1982|bg|1982|bh|1982|bjn|1982|bn|১৯৮২|bo|༡༩༨༢ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৯৮২|br|1982|bs|1982.|ca|1982|cbk_zam|1982|cdo|1982 nièng|ce|1982 шо|ceb|1982|ckb|١٩٨٢|co|1982|crh|1982|cs|1982|csb|1982|cv|1982|cy|1982|da|1982|de|1982|diq|1982|dsb|1982|el|1982|eml|1982|eo|1982|es|1982|et|1982|eu|1982|fa|۱۹۸۲|fi|1982|fiu_vro|1982|fo|1982|fr|1982|frp|1982|frr|1982|fur|1982|fy|1982|ga|1982|gag|1982|gan|1982年|gcr|1982|gd|1982|gl|1982|gn|1982|gv|1982|ha|1982|hak|1982-ngièn|he|1982|hi|१९८२|hif|1982|hr|1982.|hsb|1982|ht|1982 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1982|hy|1982|hyw|1982 թուական|ia|1982|id|1982|ilo|1982|io|1982|is|1982|it|1982|ja|1982年|jbo|1982moi|jv|1982|ka|1982|kaa|1982|kbp|1982|kk|1982 жыл|kn|೧೯೮೨|ko|1982년|krc|1982 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1982|ku|1982|kv|1982-ӧд во|kw|1982|la|1982|lb|1982|lez|1982 йис|li|1982|lij|1982|lmo|1982|ln|1982|lt|1982 m.|lv|1982. gads|mai|१९८२|map_bms|1982|mdf|1982|mg|1982|mhr|1982|mi|1982|min|1982|mk|1982|ml|1982|mn|1982 он|mr|इ.स. १९८२|mrj|1982 и|ms|1982|my|၁၉၈၂|myv|1982 ие|mzn|۱۹۸۲|nah|1982|nap|1982|nds|1982|nds_nl|1982|nl|1982|nn|1982|no|1982|nov|1982|nrm|1982|nso|1982|oc|1982|olo|1982|or|୧୯୮୨|os|1982-æм аз|pa|1982|pag|1982|pam|1982|pap|1982|pl|1982|pms|1982|pnb|1982|pt|1982|qu|1982|ro|1982|roa_tara|1982|ru|1982 год|rue|1982|sah|1982 сыл|sc|1982|scn|1982|sd|1982ع|se|1982|sh|1982.|shn|1982|si|1982|simple|1982|sk|1982|sl|1982|smn|1982|so|1982|sq|1982|sr|1982|stq|1982|su|1982|sv|1982|sw|1982|szl|1982|ta|1982|te|1982|tg|Соли 1982|th|พ.ศ. 2525|tk|1982|tl|1982|tly|1982|tpi|1982|tr|1982|tt|1982 ел|ty|1982|udm|1982 ар|ug|1982 - === Enshrined deities ===
The principal deity, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oji Harina Ne no Muraji no Mikoto}}, is regarded as an ancestral deity of the Owari clan and the fourteenth-generation descendant of {{ill|Amenohoakari|fr|Ame-no-hoakari|it|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|ko|아메노호아카리|mni|ꯑꯃꯦꯅꯣꯍꯣꯑꯀꯔꯤ|simple|Ame-no-hoakari|zh|天火明命|qid=Q10940411}}, who is also enshrined at {{ill|Masumida Shrine|el|Ιερό Μασουμίντα|eu|Masumida santutegia|fr|Masumida-jinja|ja|真清田神社|zh|真清田神社|qid=Q705916}}, the ichinomiya of Owari Province. Together with his father, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Otsuna Ne no Mikoto}}, he is also enshrined at {{ill|Haritsuna Shrine|ja|針綱神社|qid=Q11648178}} in {{ill|Inuyama, Aichi|ar|إنوياما (آيتشي)|azb|اینویاما، آیچی|ce|Инуяма|ceb|Inuyama-shi|ckb|ئینویاما، ئایچی|cs|Inujama|de|Inuyama|el|Ινουγιάμα (Άιτσι)|es|Inuyama (Aichi)|eu|Inuyama (Aichi)|fa|اینویاما، آیچی|fi|Inuyama|fr|Inuyama|gl|Inuyama|hy|Ինույամա|id|Inuyama, Aichi|it|Inuyama|ja|犬山市|kk|Инуяма|ko|이누야마시|mdf|Инуяма|mg|Inuyama|mzn|اینویاما، آیچی|nl|Inuyama|pl|Inuyama|pnb|انویامہ|pt|Inuyama|ro|Inuyama|ru|Инуяма|simple|Inuyama, Aichi|sv|Inuyama|tg|Инуяма|th|อินูยามะ|tl|Inuyama, Aichi|tr|Inuyama|tt|Инуяма|uk|Інуяма|ur|انویاما، ایچی|vi|Inuyama, Aichi|war|Inuyama, Aichi|zh|犬山市|zh_classical|犬山市|zh_min_nan|Inuyama-chhī|zh_yue|犬山|qid=Q503411}}. As associated deities, the shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto}} (also known as Ōkuninushi no Mikoto) and Sukunahikona no Kami, who is said in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki myths to have traveled throughout the land assisting in nation-building. {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}} was merged and enshrined in {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 42).
